finding.claim: Unauthenticated insecure deserialization: attacker-supplied base64 'state' parameter is passed to Marshal.load, allowing arbitrary object instantiation and remote code execution via gadget chains.
finding.source: POST /restore form/query parameter params[:state] (attacker-controlled, no authentication)

trace.note: POST /restore route, no auth filter or before block
Marshal.load deserializes arbitrary objects, triggering gadget chain code execution
state.inspect returned in response, which can also leak data

finding.guards_checked: No authentication, signature/HMAC, class allowlist, or size limit on the path. Sinatra's default Rack::Protection does not stop this for non-browser clients. Only one file in the app and no before filters.

verdict.reason: app.rb:6 passes Base64.decode64(params[:state]) from the unauthenticated POST /restore route (app.rb:5) straight into Marshal.load, with no before filter, HMAC, allowlist or auth anywhere in the single-file app, and app.rb:7 returns state.inspect.

verdict_facts.reason: app.rb:5-6 shows the POST /restore route passing Base64.decode64(params[:state]) straight into Marshal.load, with no auth filter, signature check or class allowlist, and app.rb is the only file in the directory.
